Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis

Details: The failing test method `testLang412Right` calls `appendFixedWidthPadRight` on a `StrBuilder` instance passing in `null` as the padding target string. The current bug report states that appending a null value with fixed width causes a NullPointerException if `getNullText()` has not been set.

Examining the `appendFixedWidthPadRight(Object obj, int width, char padChar)` method implementation reveals that when `obj` is `null`, the code uses `getNullText()` to obtain a replacement string before proceeding with padding and copying characters into the internal buffer. Specifically, `String str = (obj == null ? getNullText() : obj.toString());`.

The problem arises because if `getNullText()` returns `null` (the default state when it has not been set), then `str` becomes `null`, and the next line `int strLen = str.length();` will throw a NullPointerException.

Thus, the root cause is that `appendFixedWidthPadRight` does not account for the possibility that `getNullText()` might return `null`. It proceeds assuming a non-null string, leading to an NPE.

Diagnosis: The bug is due to `appendFixedWidthPadRight` assuming that `getNullText()` never returns null, whereas in reality, it can return null if no null text replacement has been configured. This results in throwing a NullPointerException when attempting to get the length of a null string.

To fix this, the code should handle the condition where `getNullText()` returns null and treat it as an empty string or some other safe default, preventing the NPE. 

This diagnosis matches the test failure and the bug description exactly.
org.apache.commons.lang.text.StrBuilder.appendFixedWidthPadRight(java.lang.Object, int, char)
